title: Intrusive Consonant
paragraphs: She was an exquisite beauty, full moon of the month of Cittirai. Her curvaceous form could break even the celibacy vows of Lord Siva. She was a blossom by age but her body was not past a bud.

She stood before a cascade and her eyes lusted upon the well-built figure of a handsome male bathing nude. Unaware of her presence, he bathed nude in the cascade which changed her flustering to a flare-up of passion.
Without bothering about her neat dress, she pounced upon the bathing man to his dismay. “My dear, why are you quivering?” The cheeky girl enquired and made her mark upon his lips.
Pushing her away, he gathered sense to wrap up the towel lying on the bank. “What did you do?” He enquired angrily.
“What wrong did I do? I was just practising the lesson learnt from the teacher!”
“Look, girl! I might be your teacher; but I am not the poet Utāraṉ of Pilkaṇīyam, nor are you Amutavalli whom Utāraṉ taught.”
“My Lord! Our names might have changed, but who would prevent us from playing the roles of Amutavalli and Utāraṉ?”
She spoke thus and embraced him again.
“Fie upon you! Leave me! Is this the way a student behaves with a teacher? Are you not ashamed?”
“That I possess in abundance - but then Cupid’s arrow burns me like fire.”
“Get away! Don’t speak irrationally!”
“Well, you only taught...?”
“What did I teach? Speak up.”

“ ‘If a word ends with a vowel to be followed by another word beginning with a vowel, uṭampaṭumei (intrusive consonant) would ensue; that form would not be disapproved by anybody but rather accepted’. This is what you taught with the example mā + ilai --> māvilai. Just have a look at us. Aren’t we a fine example of this phenomenon? When grammar endorses coalescing of uyir (vowels), why cannot it be extended to our bodies?”
“You stupid girl! Are you trying to put into practice the lesson taught? I spoke of the grammar of letters but you extend it to my neck.”
“Don’t worry, dear! I have learned my lessons in the right sense. Was there anything wrong in my understanding of Tolkāppiyam?”
“It was impeccable, but is this the place to practise it?”
“Oh! Pardon me, If place is what bothers you, there is a hall nearby.”
She dragged him and he followed her to the hall.

> Where the preceding word’s final > And the succeeding word’s beginning > Are both vowels, > The intervention of an intrusive consonant [/y/, /v/] > Is not forbidden. > > (Eḻuttatikāram : Puṇariyal, verse 38)
